question: A 28-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of a recurrent pruritic rash on his face and scalp. He reports that he has been using a new shaving cream once a week for the past 5 months. A year ago, he was diagnosed with HIV and is currently receiving triple antiretroviral therapy. He drinks several six-packs of beer weekly. Vital signs are within normal limits. A photograph of the rash is shown. A similar rash is seen near the hairline of the scalp and greasy yellow scales are seen at the margins of the eyelids. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Recurrent pruritic rash on face and scalp" -> "New shaving cream use once a week for 5 months" -> "Possibility of contact dermatitis" -> 70% CHAIN: "Greasy yellow scales at the margins of the eyelids" -> "Similar rash near hairline of the scalp" -> "Possibility of seborrheic dermatitis" -> 80% CHAIN: "Diagnosed with HIV a year ago" -> "Receiving triple antiretroviral therapy" -> "Increased risk for seborrheic dermatitis due to immunosuppression" -> 75% CHAIN: "Drinks several six-packs of beer weekly" -> "Possible exacerbation of seborrheic dermatitis due to alcohol consumption" -> 60% CHAIN: "Photograph shows rash on face" -> "Similar rash near hairline of the scalp" -> "Consistent with seborrheic dermatitis presentation" -> 70%
analysis: Based on the patient's history of HIV, use of a new shaving cream, and presentation of a pruritic rash with greasy yellow scales at the margins of the eyelids, the most likely diagnosis is seborrheic dermatitis.
